target.title: fix(whatsapp): suppress unhandled rejections from void fire-and-forget calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four fire-and-forget `void` async calls in the WhatsApp extension could produce unhandled Promise rejections when their underlying asynchronous operations failed:

- `logSelfId` called `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime().then()` without catching dynamic-import failures
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `statusReactionController.setThinking()` without catching network errors
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `finalizeWhatsAppStatusReaction()` without catching state-transition errors
- `processMessage` called `statusReactionController.setQueued()` without catching rejection

Node terminates the process on unhandled rejections, so any of these failure modes could crash the gateway during normal operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each call now uses `.catch()` to absorb the rejection. All four paths are best-effort: `logSelfId` is periodic status logging, and status reactions are non-critical lifecycle signaling. The `.catch()` pattern matches the defensive style already used across the codebase (e.g. `session.ts:232`, `login.ts:30`, `inbound/monitor.ts:1414`).

## User Impact

WhatsApp gateway no longer risks crashing due to unhandled rejections from status-reaction signaling or self-id periodic logging. No observable change to user-facing behavior.

## Evidence

**Unit test results** — each fix site has a dedicated test that makes the underlying async operation reject and confirms no crash or unhandled rejection:

```
$ pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.log-self-id.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

$ pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  54 passed (54)

$ pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

**Test methodology:**
- `channel.log-self-id.test.ts`: mocks `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime` to reject, calls `logSelfId`, flushes microtasks — passes without unhandled rejection
- `inbound-dispatch.test.ts`: passes a `StatusReactionController` mock where all state methods (`setThinking`, `setDone`, `setError`, `clear`) reject — `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` completes normally
- `process-message.test.ts`: mocks `createWhatsAppStatusReactionController` to return a controller where `setQueued()` rejects — `processMessage` completes normally
